judge_panel.matching_evidence:
In Sec. 3.1, Equation (1) defines the optimal feature set $\mathcal{F}_n^*$ using an $\arg\max$ outer loop over a $\min$ inner loop: $\arg\max_{\mathcal{F}' \in \mathcal{S}_n} [ \min \mathcal{L}(...) ]$. The text explicitly defines $\mathcal{L}$ as an "error function" (e.g., RMSE, MAE). If the inner loop minimizes the error to find the best model parameters, taking the $\arg\max$ in the outer loop seeks the feature set that *maximizes* the minimum error—thereby returning the *worst* possible feature set, not the optimal one.

The outer loop uses $\arg\max$ while the inner loop uses $\min$ on an error function $\mathcal{L}$. This incorrectly seeks the feature set that produces the highest possible error (the worst features). To find the best features, the outer loop must be an $\arg\min$ when operating over an error/loss function.
judge_panel.reasoning: This explicitly identifies Eq. (1) and says the outer optimization should be argmin rather than argmax, matching the injected identity replacement exactly.
